title: Collection-window means lost 4-5 percent of daily thermal exposure above 10 C in two Swedish insect samples from 2019
abstract: We tested the thermal exposure lost when a temperature base is applied after averaging over an insect collection window. We used 5836 measured collections in two periods each in Sweden and Madagascar in 2019-2020. At a 10 C base, the equal-trap mean loss relative to daily positive temperature excess was 4.77% and 4.01% in Sweden. Trap bootstrap ranges were 4.21-5.39% and 3.23-4.89%. Both Madagascar losses were zero. At 20 C, Madagascar losses were 4.45% and 7.28%. Loss occurs when daily temperatures cross the base within a window. Swedish loss persisted in 5-10 day collections. Splitting windows into blocks of at most seven days reduced loss but did not remove it. Equal-trap weights, measured-sample filters, common-trap checks and duration checks address parts of observation bias. These results audit a weather calculation. They do not estimate insect development, causal climate effects or pollution effects. One survey year per country, selected sites and daily mean air temperature limit wider use. The package gives code, aggregate evidence, figures, source hashes and reproduction instructions. External records stay outside the bundle.

display.caption: At a fixed 10 C base, collection-window means lose thermal exposure in both Swedish periods. Zero-proxy windows contain measured catch. Bars are equal-trap means. Ranges resample observed traps; they do not describe regional probability samples.

Loss depends on the base relative to local weather. Fractions omit trap-periods with zero total daily exposure; two early and seven late Swedish traps are omitted at 20 C. The bases are diagnostic values, not fitted biological thresholds.
